title.narrative: Improving access to food for the under-served and most vulnerable in Dinsoor district, Southwest State.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtBetween April and June 2025, an estimated 4.6 million people in Somalia are projected to face severe impacts of hunger and acute food insecurity (IPC phase 3 or higher), marking a rise from the 4.4 million previously estimated in January. Apart from dwindling availability of funds, anticipated below average Gu season (April-June) rainfall, rising food prices, continued conflict and insecurity, and localized flooding persist as key drivers of food insecurity (WFP Somalia Country Brief, March 2025)?In early 2025, cereal prices in Dinsoor showed mixed trends, influenced by then Deyr harvests and localized market factors. Dinsoor’s market functions but has vulnerabilities. Road re-openings in 2025 have stabilized supply chains, with regular deliveries of staples and fuel from Mogadishu and Baidoa, replacing previously limited air or informal routes (WFP Fortnight Market Supply Chain Update 16-30 Apr 2025). READO also consulted local communities in Dinsoor to identify the needs for food security and identified a couple of gaps including negative coping strategies among the IDPs and host community. READO employed desk review and Key Informant Interviews (KIIs) to collect date on the needs in Dinsoor. Overall, Dinsoor’s markets are now integrated enough to support cash-based assistance. ?ltbrgtIn response READO plans to improve food access for 5430 individuals (905HHs, both IDPs Host community). Of these, 500 HHs will receive unconditional cash transfers-UCT for 3 monthly cycles at $55/month (70% MEB), while 405HHs will receive conditional cash-for-work transfers for 4 months. Transfers will be done via mobile money a PDM will assess the UCT process. READO will coordinate with the FSC, CCCM, WASH, Nutrition, and partners to avoid duplication/overlap of activities. In line with the SHF Allocation Strategy, convergence will be ensured through joint community mobilization and beneficiary selection, promoting maximum sector integration and minimizing inclusion/exclusion errors. ?Furthermore, this project will ensure protection mainstreaming by prioritising the safety, dignity, and equitable access of all beneficiaries throughout program design and implementation. Activities will be planned with community participation to identify and mitigate risks,avoid harm, and address barriers faced by marginalized groups. Disability inclusion will be integral, with tailored work roles and accommodations ensuring persons with disabilities can participate safely and meaningfully. The beneficiary selection criteria and targeting processes will actively include women, youth, the elderly, and people with disabilities to prevent exclusion. PSEA will be embedded across all activities through staff training, strict codes of conduct, PDM questions, and clear contractual clauses with suppliers. READO confidential, accessible feedback and complaint mechanisms will enable beneficiaries to report concerns safely. PSEA awareness materials will be widely displayed, and a dedicated focal point will monitor and respond to risks promptly.?ltbrgtREADO has a strong presence in Southwest State and has implemented Food Security and WASH projects in Dinsoor previously, hence bearing operational capacity to directly implement. In addition, READO has a strong knowledge of the local context and developed a good rapport with the local administration and communities. READO will build on this good rapport to respond quickly to the needs. In addition, READO has the added advantage of being an LNGO, and it implements its activities through local staff with high knowledge and experience Somalia's context and clan dynamics. READO will ensure community engagement in all phases of the project, particularly women's participation .?The following are the target locations among the IDP and host communities in Dinsoor: Hubey, Easow, Towfiq, Abdalla Hassan, Ala dacar-hilac, Billow alla, Haja nina, and Alinoor Ali Barakowltbrgtlt/pgt
